# Design Issues (the book)

> A book made from Tim Berners-Lee's Design Issues notes
> (https://www.w3.org/DesignIssues/), edited by Melvin Carvalho.
> 96 chapters in ten volumes, in a reading order, each with its source,
> its context, and a note on what happened since.
> Editorial matter CC BY-SA 4.0; quoted material (c) Tim Berners-Lee.

## What this is and is not

This is commentary, not a reprint. The 97 source notes remain at
w3.org/DesignIssues and every chapter links to the one it discusses.
The notes are Berners-Lee's personal notes and are not endorsed by W3C.
Nothing in this book should be attributed to him except material shown as a
quotation with a citation.

## Why it exists

The Design Issues notes are the closest thing the Web has to a statement of
its architecture by its designer. They were written between 1996 and 2024 as
each question arose, never arranged for a new reader, and their author says
in his own preface that looking for an order of concepts in them offers "as
much hope as you would with words in the dictionary." This book supplies the
order: every note gets exactly one chapter, placed so that terms are defined
before use.

## Structure

Ten volumes, graded by the kind of claim each makes:

- Volume I, Axioms (Ch 1-6): design commitments argued from first needs.
  Principles of design, the URI axioms, the name/address myth, the Web model
  and its independence axioms, the 50,000-foot survey, net/web/graph layering.
- Volume II, Naming (Ch 7-15): architectural fact, checkable against the URI
  and HTTP specifications. What HTTP URIs identify, generic resources,
  fragments, relative URIs, persistence, URI ownership.
- Volume III, Evolution (Ch 16-26): how a deployed system changes without
  breaking. Evolvability, extensible languages, mandatory extensions,
  modularity, the specification stack, ambiguity, HTML and XML, openness,
  webizing.
- Volume IV, Meaning (Ch 27-39): proposal and specification. Metadata
  architecture, document meaning, the Semantic Web roadmap, RDF against XML
  and against relational models, identity, labels, interpretation.
- Volume V, Logic and Notation (Ch 40-48): rules, inference, Notation3 and
  the alternatives considered, reification, RDF diff, inconsistency.
- Volume VI, Linked Data and Solid (Ch 49-65): the four rules, read-write
  Linked Data, government and science data, Solid, pods, human-data
  interfaces, shapes and footprints, live data, feeds, web services.
- Volume VII, Trust (Ch 66-74): the contested present, attributed and dated.
  Real trust, the HTTPS Everywhere objection, same-origin granularity,
  client certificates, CORS, snooping, private data, the intimacy gradient.
- Volume VIII, Law (Ch 75-81): normative argument, dated. Links and laws,
  filtering, net neutrality, top-level domains, DRM, blockchain.
- Volume IX, Interface and Society (Ch 82-91): the editor that should have
  existed, user agents, fractal society, cultures, social network
  dysfunction.
- Volume X, Futures (Ch 92-96): disciplined speculation, labeled as such by
  its author. Beneficent apps, Charlie, Singularity 13, a vision of a new
  world.

## Chapter shape

Every chapter carries: a source note naming the original title, date, length
and URL; inline SVG figures where a picture shows the mechanism better than
prose; "The question", giving the argument it was written into; the
argument restated in order with quotations attributed and cited; "What
happened since", listing outcomes with specification numbers and dates;
"Connections" to other chapters; and four questions.

## Status

Volumes I to V are written (chapters 1-48, half the book). Chapters 49-96
are stubs carrying their place in the order and a link to their source. Volumes are written in order. Anything
marked "in preparation" has no prose yet and should not be cited.

## Files

- /index.html - title page, volume overview, full table of contents
- /chapters/NN-slug.html - one chapter each, numbered in reading order
- /README.md - contribution front door and house standards
- Source: https://github.com/DesignIssues/design-issues
